Let <MATH_0001> be a scheme.
Let <MATH_0002> be a property of morphisms of algebraic spaces over <MATH_0003>.
Assume
<STRUCT_0001>
<STRUCT_0002> <MATH_0004> is smooth local on the source,
<STRUCT_0003> <MATH_0005> is smooth local on the target, and
<STRUCT_0004> <MATH_0006> is stable under postcomposing with smooth morphisms:
if <MATH_0007> has <MATH_0008> and <MATH_0009> is a smooth morphism
then <MATH_0010> has <MATH_0011>.
<STRUCT_0005>
Then <MATH_0012> is smooth local on the source-and-target.

Let <MATH_0001> be a property of morphisms of algebraic spaces which
satisfies conditions (1), (2) and (3) of the lemma. By
Lemma <REF_0001>
we see that <MATH_0002> is stable under precomposing with
smooth morphisms. By
Lemma <REF_0002>
we see that <MATH_0003> is stable under smooth base change.
Hence it suffices to prove part (3) of
Definition <REF_0003>
holds.

<STRUCT_0001><STRUCT_0002>
More precisely, suppose that <MATH_0004> is a morphism
of algebraic spaces over <MATH_0005> which satisfies
Definition <REF_0004> part (3)(b).
In other words, for every <MATH_0006> there exists a smooth
morphism <MATH_0007>, a point <MATH_0008> mapping to <MATH_0009>,
a smooth morphism <MATH_0010>, and a morphism <MATH_0011>
such that <MATH_0012> and <MATH_0013> has <MATH_0014>.
The proof of the lemma is complete once we show that <MATH_0015> has <MATH_0016>.
Set <MATH_0017>, <MATH_0018>, <MATH_0019>,
<MATH_0020>, and <MATH_0021>. We obtain a
commutative diagram
<MATH_0022>
with <MATH_0023>, <MATH_0024> smooth, <MATH_0025> surjective. Note that <MATH_0026> has <MATH_0027>
as each <MATH_0028> does and <MATH_0029> is smooth local on the target.
Because <MATH_0030> is surjective and <MATH_0031> is smooth local on the source,
it suffices to prove that <MATH_0032> has <MATH_0033>.
This follows as we assumed that <MATH_0034> is stable under
postcomposing with a smooth morphism and as <MATH_0035> is smooth.
